note:
Second round for the REVIEWS page hero. Malcolm on round one: 'too standard and too boring - we need closer shots and the models should be smiling a little more - try greater variation of position and shot angle - and all of them should be closer to the face.'

WHAT MADE ROUND ONE BORING, DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN GUESSED. Round one told every slot that the head 'reaches about three quarters of the frame height and sits clear of both the top and the bottom edge', with an even graphite ground filling the other two thirds. That is the literal specification of a corporate headshot on a seamless backdrop, and eleven of eleven candidates duly delivered one. The engines were not being unimaginative - they were being obedient.

THE CROP HAPPENS TWICE, AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF ROUND TWO FORGOT THE SECOND ONE. Round two's first draft said the top of the head is cut by the upper edge and the chin by the lower edge, so the face filled the master top to bottom. Rendered in the live box that was a disaster and only an in-situ test caught it: the theme keeps the middle 68.75% of a 3:1 master, and only 54% of a 21:9 one, so a face that already fills its master loses everything outside a central strip. Five of five candidates checked in place showed eyes and a nose with THE SMILE CROPPED AWAY BELOW THE FRAME - the one element Malcolm asked for more of.

SO CLOSENESS IS BOUGHT HORIZONTALLY, NOT VERTICALLY. Every slot now places the face across the width and holds the eyes and the smiling mouth inside the central horizontal band of the master, with hair or shadow above and jaw or shadow below as the sacrificial margin. The face still occupies about sixty per cent of the master's height, which after the theme's crop fills roughly 87% of the 440px banner - a genuinely tight shot in the place it actually gets seen, rather than a tight shot that survives only in the file.

That band instruction is written pictorially - 'her eyes sit just above the middle of the picture' - never as 'safe area' or 'will be cropped'. Brief words describing the brief have been printed into the artwork as label text on this project before.

BEAUTIFUL AS WELL AS REAL. The first draft paired hard raking light with macro pore language and several candidates came back reading as dermatology documentation rather than beauty photography. Light is soft-directional throughout now and the skin line asks for radiant and luminous as well as real, with unflattering / harsh clinical lighting / dermatology photograph negated.

SMILING MORE. Round one's closed-lip half read as neutral once the 40% overlay went over it. Every slot here carries an unmistakable smile with the cheeks lifted and the eyes creased; five open with teeth, three closed-lip but generous. The smile is a constant, not a variable.

ANGLE IS THE VARIABLE. Camera height and head axis change in every slot: level, from below, from above, pure profile, diagonal, back over the shoulder, half the face cropped away, tipped back from above.

GEOMETRY AND SUPPLIERS. Still 3:1 so all six run - gpt-image hard-refuses past 3:1, and only Seedream reaches the eventual 4.41:1 master. Choice round first, widen the winner afterwards. Mobile still needs its own companion in the section's mobile_image slot; an off-centre face does not survive the phone crop.

slots.title: Camera level, face spans the width, open smile to lens
slots.prompt: Extremely tight macro beauty photograph of one beautiful woman about thirty six years old, of Northern European appearance with fair skin, in a very wide cinematic frame three times wider than it is tall. The camera is at eye level and very close - her face is large enough that it spans more than half the width of the picture and runs off the right edge. Her eyes sit just above the middle of the picture and her smiling mouth just below it, so that both are held well inside the central horizontal band of the frame; the top fifth of the frame is dark hair and shadow above her brow, and the bottom fifth is the shadowed underside of her jaw. She is smiling broadly and genuinely with her lips parted and her upper teeth showing, her cheeks pushed up and the outer corners of her eyes creased into warm folds, looking straight into the lens. The left third of the picture is the shadowed side of her cheek and the dark air beside it, falling to near-black and even in tone with no detail in it. One soft directional light from the far right glances across the cheekbone and the bridge of the nose so the lit side glows. Skin is real, radiant and finely textured - healthy and luminous, with fine down catching the light and the natural creases a real smile makes at the eyes and beside the mouth present and lit rather than erased. Very shallow depth of field with the near eye critically sharp, fine film grain, editorial, intimate, high contrast.
